derivation: Four points, and a warning about the three lines between them. The train was assembled in Moscow on the night of 7-8 August 1918 (Trotsky's own date); it stood at Sviyazhsk from about 10 August, though the day of arrival is nowhere given in what could be read here; it was there for the retaking of Kazan on 10 September; and its guard detachment fought at Petrograd during Yudenich's drive in October 1919, for which the train was decorated. Everything between those points is unrecorded here.
notes: By Trotsky's own count the train made thirty-six journeys and covered more than 105,000 kilometres. This track shows four positions and about 2,400 kilometres of straight line, which is a little over two per cent of it. **It is not an itinerary and must not be read as one.** It is here because the train is the pack's central object - in a war with no front, command means going there - and because showing four documented stops is more honest than either drawing a route nobody has reconstructed or leaving out the most important vehicle in the war.
